{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Texas cuisine|Texas cuisine]]

'''Pedernales River Chili''' was American President Lyndon Johnson's favorite [[cookbook:chili con carne|chili con carne]] recipe. It was named after the location of his Texas Hill Country ranch. The recipe calls for leaving out the traditional [[Cookbook:Beef|beef]] [[Cookbook:Suet|suet]] (on doctor's orders after his heart attack while he was U.S. Senate Majority Leader) and also adds [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]] and [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]]. LBJ preferred [[Cookbook:Venison|venison]], when available, over beef; Hill Country deer were thought to be leaner than most. Lady Bird Johnson, the First Lady, had it printed up on cards as a mail-out because of the many thousands of requests the White House received for the recipe.

The recipe is originally from Zephyr Wright, the Johnson's family cook.

==Ingredients==
*4 [[Cookbook:Pound|lbs]] (1.8 {{kg}}) coarse-ground [[Cookbook:Meat|meat]] ([[Cookbook:venison|venison]] preferred)
*1 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*2 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], finely chopped
*1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] dried [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]] (preferable to fresh [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]], which grows wild in central Texas)
*1 teaspoon powdered [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
*6 teaspoons [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|chili powder]] (or more, to taste)
*2 cans (16-[[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]/500[[Cookbook:g|g]]) whole [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]] 
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste
*2 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (470 [[Cookbook:mL|ml]]) hot water

==Procedure==
#[[cookbook:browning|Brown]] meat, onion, and garlic in a large [[Cookbook:skillet|skillet]]. 
#Add rest of ingredients and bring to a boil. Lower heat, cover, and [[Cookbook:simmer|simmer]] for about an hour. 
#Skim off grease.
